A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, algorithms and experiments. All pages, including Appendices A-C, are readable and support reliable comparison despite changes in pagination.

before.justification: v3 reports original Gaussian-mixture and MuJoCo experiments, computational measurements, sensitivity analyses and a Two Moon experiment in Appendix C.4.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix C, including benchmark returns and generated samples.

M1.justification: The RSM loss family, DPMD and SDAC objectives, reverse sampling procedure and Algorithms 1-2 are unchanged. The revised mathematical derivations do not establish a change to the proposed procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten MuJoCo v4 tasks, Gaussian-mixture sampling and Two Moon sampling. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains PPO, TD3, SAC, QSM, DIPO, DACER, QVPO and DPPO. The Gaussian-mixture comparison retains DSM and Langevin dynamics, while the Two Moon comparison retains DDPM, iDEM and FAB.

E3.justification: Both report 200k iterations and one million environment interactions, with fivefold budgets for Humanoid. Evaluation cadence, 20-episode return averages, model settings and Appendix C's experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 retains the same Ant sensitivity analyses comparing 10, 20 and 30 diffusion steps and linear, variance-preserving and cosine schedules. No additional or removed ablation, robustness test or case study was found.

E5.justification: Table 1 and Figure 3 retain the same reporting of means and standard deviations across five random seeds. Appendix C.5's repeated-run information is unchanged, with no new statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 and Figures 2-5 retain identical results, including DPMD's Humanoid return of 6959 ± 460 and Ant return of 5683 ± 138. Computational measurements, sampling findings and sensitivity trends are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix B.1 replace the direct squared-error derivation with a proof explicitly defining the posterior distribution and invoking Tweedie's identity. Appendix B.2.1 now applies Proposition 3.1 directly and corrects action indices from a to a_0. The theorem's conclusion and final reweighted objectives remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient diffusion-policy training without target-policy samples, the DPMD/SDAC algorithms and their empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Interpretations of baseline failures, sampling and computation advantages, sensitivity results and the Two Moon comparison are retained. The discussion of future improvements to stability and exploration is also unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed JAX implementation link, workstation specifications, pseudocode and hyperparameter tables are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same training and baseline implementation details.

R1.justification: v4 adds Efron (2011) to support Tweedie's identity and removes Section 3.1's explicit sentence crediting the score-matching connection to Vincent (2011). Vincent remains cited in Appendix A and the bibliography; broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Proof exposition in Section 3.1 and Appendices B.1-B.2 is locally rewritten, alongside small punctuation, list-label and equation-reference edits. The overall section structure and most prose are preserved.

P2.justification: Reformatted proof displays cause local text reflow, and Table 2 and Figure 4 move from the left to the right column on page 9. All figures and tables retain their content and structure; no display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The explicit posterior-score identity and revised DPMD derivation improve traceability. However, v4 introduces an inconsistent posterior-sampling subscript in main-text Equation (11), listing a_t instead of a_0, while Appendix B.1 retains the missing factor 2 in the squared-error cross term already present in v3. These explanatory gains and notation/algebra defects leave the net quality direction uncertain; methods and empirical evidence are unchanged.
